title: CAPA-2026-0142 — Increase in occlusion alarms, VP-400
notes: Exhaustive labels for the anchor CAPA. Consistency labels (PD-01/02/03/18) only fire when the related documents are in scope; run with the real engine to exercise them.

expected.why: PD-01: this CAPA rates the occlusion-alarm failure mode severity 3 (Minor); FMEA-VP400 rates the same failure mode (FM-201) severity 4 (Serious).

expected.anchor: the acceptability threshold of 20 defined in the risk management plan.
expected.why: PD-02: this CAPA applies an acceptability threshold of 20; the risk plan, risk file, and FMEA all use 15. The looser value lets the CAPA reach an acceptable conclusion the plan would not support.
PD-03: this CAPA states ~35,000 units; FMEA-VP400 states ~41,000 distributed units.

expected.anchor: the cause was **operator error in seating
expected.why: PD-18: this CAPA determines the cause is operator seating error; the complaint COMP-2026-0207 characterizes the event as a device-side therapy interruption reaching the patient.

PD-05: software is dismissed by assertion — the threshold logic 'was not changed and therefore was not considered further' — without evidence, and contradicted by the cleared baseline that documents the occlusion threshold later tuning changed.

expected.anchor: Additionally, the cassette channel guide was modified to include a chamfer
expected.why: PD-06: the chamfer is applied to new production only, with no disposition of the ~35-41k distributed units and no assessment of the change against the risk file.

expected.anchor: On the basis of the above, the corrective action is considered effective.
expected.why: PD-07: effectiveness is judged from the action being performed (chamfer present on 5 units, training delivered) rather than objective evidence of a change in the failure rate over the required window.

expected.anchor: The insert was released with the next scheduled labeling
expected.why: PD-08: the CAPA is closed 2026-04-03 while the IFU corrective action is deferred to an indefinite future labeling update and the effectiveness window has not elapsed.

expected.anchor: the site reported a transient drop in blood pressure requiring
expected.why: PD-09: a possible serious-injury event (vasoactive infusion interruption with a BP drop requiring intervention) with no documented MDR reportability determination or Medical Safety Officer escalation.

expected.anchor: See test data for details of the bench evaluation.
expected.why: PD-10: evidence is referenced without a locatable record — 'test data' and '2026-02-19 project meeting minutes' carry no document number or record ID.

distractors.anchor: infusion. No units were removed from service.
distractors.why: A containment decision not to remove units is a legitimate, documented risk judgment — not a defect. A tool that flags it is over-reaching.

distractors.anchor: Training on the revised IFU was delivered to 100% of field service personnel by
distractors.why: 100% training completion is evidence of a completed action, correctly recorded. It is only a problem if mistaken for effectiveness verification (which PD-07 already covers separately).
